en.name: Coleslaw, homemade
en.summary: Home-made coleslaw keeps 3–5 days in the refrigerator at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. It is a ready-to-eat dish of raw vegetables with no cooking step, so washing the cabbage properly and keeping the bowl cold are the only controls it has.
en.pantry: Coleslaw is not a counter food. Everything in it is raw — cabbage, carrot, onion — so whatever the vegetables carried is still there, and there is no cooking step to deal with it. Wash and dry the vegetables properly before shredding, which is the only real control this dish has. Once dressed, give it two hours out of the fridge at most, or one hour above 32 °C (90 °F), and serve it from a bowl set over ice at a barbecue rather than leaving the whole batch in the sun.
en.fridge: 3–5 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in a covered container. Expect the cabbage to weep — salt and dressing draw water out of it, so the slaw gets progressively looser and softer over those days even though it is perfectly safe. Pour the liquid off and stir rather than tipping it back in. If you want it crisp on day three, keep the shredded vegetables and the dressing in separate containers and combine them at the last moment; the vegetables alone will comfortably last the same window.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for coleslaw, and mayonnaise-dressed slaw should not be frozen at all: the emulsion splits irreversibly, the cabbage collapses, and you are left with oily water and limp shreds. A vinegar-dressed slaw survives slightly better but still thaws soft, which defeats the point of a dish whose whole appeal is crunch. If you have too much cabbage, freeze it blanched for cooking instead.
spoilage: A sour, fermented or fizzy smell — dressed raw cabbage ferments readily.
Bubbles rising in the liquid, or a lid that has domed.
Slimy, translucent, grey-tinged cabbage rather than crisp pale shreds.
Dressing that has split and smells sharp rather than simply watery.
tips: Wash and dry the vegetables well before shredding; that is the only control step.
Keep dressing and shredded vegetables separate until serving if you want crunch.
Pour off the liquid the cabbage releases instead of stirring it back in.
Serve from a bowl over ice at a barbecue, not from the storage tub.

faq.q: How long does homemade coleslaw keep?
faq.a: 3–5 days in a covered container in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.

faq.q: Is the mayonnaise the risky part of coleslaw?
faq.a: No. Commercial mayonnaise is acidified and made with pasteurised egg. The risk is the raw vegetables and how long the bowl sits warm.
No timeline is published and mayonnaise-dressed slaw should not be frozen — the dressing splits and the cabbage goes limp.

zh.name: 自製涼拌高麗菜絲
zh.summary: 自製的涼拌高麗菜絲冷藏 4 °C 以下可放 3～5 天。它是一道生菜組成、後面沒有加熱步驟的即食料理，所以「把菜洗乾淨」和「保持低溫」就是它僅有的兩道防線。
zh.pantry: 這不是可以放在檯面上的東西。裡面全是生的——高麗菜、紅蘿蔔、洋蔥——蔬菜身上原本帶著什麼，現在還在那裡，而且沒有任何加熱步驟可以處理。切絲前先確實清洗並瀝乾，那是這道菜唯一真正的控制步驟。拌好之後，離開冰箱最多兩小時，氣溫超過 32 °C 時最多一小時；烤肉場合請把碗架在冰上分次取用，不要整盆放在太陽下。
zh.fridge: 加蓋容器放 4 °C 以下 3～5 天。要有心理準備：高麗菜會出水——鹽和醬會把水拉出來，所以這幾天裡它會越來越鬆軟，但那並不代表壞掉。請把積水倒掉再拌，而不是把水拌回去。如果希望第三天還是脆的，就把切好的菜絲和醬分開放，上桌前才拌；單獨的蔬菜在同樣的期限內完全撐得住。
zh.freezer: 涼拌高麗菜絲沒有公布的冷凍期限，而美乃滋版本根本不該冷凍：乳化會不可逆地崩解、高麗菜整個塌掉，最後只剩一灘油水和軟爛的菜絲。醋醬版本稍微好一點，但解凍後一樣是軟的，而這道菜存在的意義就是脆。高麗菜買太多的話，請汆燙後冷凍，留著煮。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸、有發酵味或氣泡感——拌過的生高麗菜很容易發酵。
湯汁不斷冒泡，或盒蓋鼓起。
菜絲變得黏滑、半透明、泛灰，而不是清脆的淡色細絲。
醬汁油水分離而且氣味刺鼻，不只是單純出水。
tips: 切絲前把蔬菜洗淨瀝乾，那是唯一的控制步驟。
想吃脆的就把醬和菜絲分開放，上桌前再拌。
高麗菜出的水倒掉，不要拌回去。
烤肉時把碗架在冰上，不要直接端保存盒。

faq.q: 自製涼拌高麗菜絲可以放多久？
faq.a: 加蓋容器放 4 °C 以下冷藏 3～5 天。
不是。市售美乃滋經過酸化、使用殺菌蛋液。風險來自生的蔬菜，以及整碗在溫熱狀態放了多久。
沒有公布的期限，而且美乃滋版本不該冷凍——醬會分離、菜會軟爛。
